hook: SCP-2790 opens like a cute joke file about a squid that everyone is supposed to cuddle, with an object class of BFF. Read it slowly and keep track of what the procedures actually tell staff to do, line by line. It ends in surgical body horror, delivered in exactly the same cheerful tone.
whyItMatters: This is an article that lets its voice carry the story. The bubbly phrasing, the gushing adjectives and the strange statistics accumulate until the way the report is written becomes more unsettling than anything it describes. It shows how far a format built on clinical detachment can be bent just by changing the mood of whoever seems to be writing it.
thingsToNotice: The numbers give it away: the breach rate goes from zero to zero and is reported both as a rise and as a fall, and complications affecting 87% of grafted staff are described as 'only' minor. Necrosis around the grafts is read as the body discarding its own imperfect skin, while the staff's natural skin is described in increasingly ugly terms. By the last addendum everyone at Site-54 has 2790's skin on their hands, and there are plans to replace all of their skin with it. The closing note says the site is now quarantined and the page was kept as a lesson in screening new acquisitions for memetic and cognitohazardous effects, which puts everything above in a very different light.
